cells.tense: The ending is being finished now, and your hand is steady on it, among the people who share the practice.
cells.act: adjust the share until it is fair, then stop
cells.ask: At a gathering where the load sits lopsided — same person hosting, same person telling the old story — adjust what you take on until the shares come level, then stop.
cells.core:
Among the people who share a practice, a thing can finish when it's finished — a ritual gone thin, a custom held since before anyone remembers — without the ending turning into a fight. What you keep walking with weighs less for what you set down, and the people at the table notice.

When the next gathering circles something worn through, don't settle it by yourself. Someone usually carries more of it than anyone sees. Say what you're carrying, ask what the others carry, and adjust the shares until they come level. No one has to win, and nobody keeps score. What closes after that belongs to the people it touched, and it lands the way a fair exchange lands — quietly, without announcement.
cells.sheetLine: A tradition can end without breaking what it carried.
cells.verb: Letting what is finished end, so what is alive can start
cells.place: In the shared meaning a group carries and passes on — rituals, customs, the words everybody knows

cells.tense: You will be clearing something shared before it has lived, and bracing for the clearing before it comes.
cells.act: let yourself be reached by what they are carrying
cells.ask: Before you call the next shared thing finished, stay through one gathering of it and let what it holds for someone at that table land on you.
cells.core:
A shared practice keeps getting closed out before it's had its run. From where you stand it looks used up, and where you stand runs a season beyond where the others are; the clearing reads as freedom from in here. Seen from the room, it reads as nothing allowed to stay long enough to mean anything. The people around it have started keeping their own things back.

What's thin isn't restraint — it's contact. Before the next clearing, stay inside a living practice alongside the people it holds, and let what it's carrying for them land on you. You don't have to fix it or agree with it. Stay long enough to feel it. The endings you make afterwards are fewer, and the right ones.
cells.sheetLine: You're clearing the table before anyone's eaten.
cells.verb: Letting what is finished end, so what is alive can start

cells.tense: You kept a shared practice past its end, and you're still standing where it used to be, holding the old form.
cells.act: go where the feeling is already pulling
cells.ask: Follow what already tugs at you this week — a craft, a walk, a skill you've wanted to start — and go there today, before the old hour pulls you back.
cells.core:
A shared practice has ended and you're keeping it on the calendar as if it hadn't. The old words still get said, the same hour still gets held, and the thing itself stopped. Keeping it going draws on hours that something alive could use.

Put a wanted thing where the dead one sits. There's a slot the old practice holds — an evening, a season, a habit of showing up — and something you actually want can go there. Follow what already tugs at you today, before the old slot pulls you back. The finished thing ends by being replaced rather than killed, and nobody needs to be told; the hour is simply full of something else.

cells.tense: Something shared is thinning under your hand, and if asked you'd say you hadn't touched it.
cells.act: give the mess a shape it can be carried in
cells.ask: Give the old way a shape you can carry for now — how often it gets done, or where it stops — and hold that without telling the group.
cells.core:
Something is already ending among the people who share it — a way of gathering, a story the group tells about itself — and the one letting it go, gently, by not renewing it, is you. Ask and you'd say you hadn't noticed. The ending has an author. The author isn't signing.

Give it a shape you can carry. Decide for yourself how often the old way gets done, or the point where it stops, and hold that without announcing anything. The thinning others can feel becomes an ending with edges on it, and the edges are in your hand. If someone asks, you have something to give them, which is more than a thinning has.
